results.title: Production LLM Systems - What Actually Breaks (And How to Fix It) – Research – Etiq AI
results.content: Production demands more than impressive outputs-it requires systems that handle real users, unexpected scenarios, and the messy complexity of actual business operations. Successful production teams implement comprehensive prompt evaluation protocols: A/B testing different variants, version control for prompt iterations, and specific metrics measuring prompt effectiveness. Consider what you're actually testing when evaluating RAG systems. Robustness testing evaluates how systems perform when things go wrong. These frameworks reconceptualize testing as combinatorial optimization problems, enabling thorough evaluation of model behavior under diverse perturbation scenarios. Effective production systems require comprehensive testing toolboxes with multiple integrated components. Architecture spans model diagnostics and performance monitoring to security testing and business metrics integration. LLM testing demands significant computational resources, making tiered approaches essential: lightweight tests for frequent execution, moderate complexity tests for daily runs, comprehensive evaluation suites for weekly or pre-release cycles, and continuous production monitoring. The testing landscape continues evolving as LLM capabilities expand and production requirements become more sophisticated.

results.content: # Benchmarking Neural Network Robustness to Common Corruptions and Perturbations. Most work on robustness in deep learning methods for vision has focused on the important challenges of robustness to adversarial examples (Szegedy et al., 2014; Carlini & Wagner, 2017; 2016), unknown unknowns (Hendrycks et al., 2019; Hendrycks & Gimpel, 2017b; Liu et al., 2018), and model or data poisoning (Steinhardt et al., 2017; Hendrycks et al., 2018). Specifically, we introduce the ImagetNet-C dataset for input *corruption robustness* and the ImageNet-P dataset for input *perturbation robustness*. These algorithmically generated corruptions are applied to the ImageNet (Deng et al., 2009) validation images to produce our corruption robustness dataset ImageNet-C. Appearing more subtly than the corruption from ImageNet-C, the Gaussian noise perturbation sequence begins with the clean ImageNet image. The goal of ImageNet-C and ImageNet-P is to evaluate the robustness of machine learning algorithms on novel corruptions and perturbations. Directly fitting the types of ImageNet-C corruptions should be avoided, as it would cause researchers to overestimate a model’s robustness.
